rules: Historian/theory/mixed are editorial scholarly-function classifications, not a ranking of intellectual worth or rigid professional membership.
Canadian-history focus follows selected works and current curated contexts, not birthplace, citizenship or employer. Marx is theory; Goffman and philosopher Charles Taylor remain theory.

Canadian-history historians: ≥150 exact dated first-author bibliography-key dissertations. Other historians: >100. Theory and mixed scholarship require their own editorial review, with counts preserved.
All source_key/count pairs retained exactly; author-key variants are not added, and namesake holds are not accepted as one-person totals.
No graph promotion, identity repair, citation recount, live publication or changes to the raw 173-row list are performed.
The identity scan checks salient conflicting works and broad keys, not every underlying citation. Absence of a hold flag is not complete external identity resolution.

threshold_tradeoff.qualification: Screening at 150 reduces the advantage conferred by Canada-heavy corpus coverage, but omits important Canadian scholarship such as Nancy Christie 149 and Strong-Boag 136. It is a prioritization aid, not a merit boundary. Carter 152 qualifies. Mixed/identity cases remain separate regardless numeric threshold.
